items.evidence: play --ticks 1 on a fresh --settings folder: screen title, one JSON object with every key the brief names (tick..ledger). The README command (path .../work) also ran as written.
README frame command wrote readme_frame.png; `file` reports PNG 800 x 480. Every frame taken later was 800x480 too.
Fresh place: texts [Night Market, Layout, Ledger, Settings, Quit], menu_index 0; 0:up keeps it at 0; downs at 1..5 reach 3 and stay there; an up at 6 gives 2.

In Settings, volume starts at 5. Seven Rights stop at 10 and eleven Lefts stop at 0. Difficulty goes Normal->Hard (stays Hard)->Normal->Easy (stays Easy). Texts read 'Volume: 2' and 'Difficulty: Hard'; Escape goes to the title.
Second run on the same --settings starts with volume 2 and hard (shown in Settings and in its frame). A fresh folder starts with 5 and normal.
0:enter on a fresh place: layout, cursor (0,0), piece stove, slot 1, stock 3/4/2, grid []. Texts: Layout, Piece: Stove, Slot: 1, Stove: 3, Table: 4, Lamp: 2, plus the Enter and Escape lines.

Inputs 2:right,3:right,4:right moved the cursor only to (1,0), and 6:up,7:up only to (1,1). Even 5:right,7:right,... with nothing between moved once in total. Only with 'none' between each word did it reach (7,4) and back to (0,0), stopping at the edges, with menu_index 0 and still in layout. So the cursor does not move one cell for each word.
2:next_piece,4:next_piece,6:next_piece stopped at table (texts 'Piece: Table'), and three prev_piece did the same. Only with 'none' between did it cycle stove,table,lamp,stove and back.

Stoves placed at (0,0),(1,0),(2,0) with stock 3->0; a 4th at (3,0) changed nothing. A table on the occupied (2,0) changed nothing. Four tables took the stock to 0 and a 5th changed nothing. Two lamps, and a 3rd changed nothing.

erase on the empty (7,3) changed nothing; erase of the lamp at (7,2) gave lamp stock 0->1; in a later run, erase of the table at (2,1) gave table stock 0->1. Grid and 'Lamp: 1'/'Table: 1' texts followed.
escape at 35 -> title; enter at 36 -> layout, cursor (0,0), same grid. A later run on the same place, 0:enter, showed the same 8 pieces and stock.

next_slot 1->2->3->1. save_slot filled slots[0] and later slots[1] and left the grid as it was. load_slot on empty slot 3 changed nothing. load_slot on slot 1 replaced the 3-piece grid with the 2-piece one, table stock 2->3.
A second run on the same place showed both slots; next_slot then load_slot gave slot 2's grid (S00,T10,T11), table stock 2.

Enter with an empty grid, and again with only a stove: stays in layout with 'Needs a stove and a table' added, and the line goes at the next word. With a stove and a table: night, clock 0, slow, 0/0/0, grid unchanged, texts include '18:00' and 'Speed: Slow'.

Night started by enter at 8: clock 1 at tick 32, 2 at 56. Fast at 60: clock 3 at 65, 4 at 71, 5 at 77. Stop at 80: clock 5 through tick 200, screen night. Slow at 200: clock 6 at 212, which keeps the 12 progress already gone. Time and Speed texts followed.
Seed 1 gives [5,12,18,...,356]: gaps all 4..10, all under 360, the same list at tick 600 and in other seed-1 runs. Seed 2 [5,9,13,...] repeated identically; seed 7 differed.

Tables (1,1),(1,3),(3,0): customer 1 went to (1,1), customer 2 to (1,3), customer 3 to (3,0); customer 4 was queued with x,y null. Separately, at minute 33 with 3 queued, the arrival was turned away and lost became 1 at that minute.
Stove (0,0) beside table (1,0): customer 1 cooking at minute 5 and eating at minute 25. Stove (0,0) with table (2,0): cooking at 5, still cooking at 34, eating at 35.
No lamp: paid at minute 35, coins 8, served 1, table taken by the next customer. Lamp at (2,1) beside table (2,0): paid at minute 45, coins 12.

Hard, stove not next to the table: customer 1 (arrived 5) is gone at 35, lost +1, no coins. Normal: customer 2 (arrived 12) leaves at 52 and customer 3 is cooking on that stove the same minute. Easy: customer 2 stays and is eating at 55.
At minute 35 customer 1 pays and customer 2, front of the queue, is already seated and cooking at (1,0) in that same minute (queue 3->2).
Clock 359 at tick 8640; at 8641 summary, clock 360, texts Night over / Coins: 24 / Served: 3 / Lost: 49 / Enter: title. Lost stayed 49 with 4 still in the stall. Enter -> title.
Same grid, seed 1, normal: slow gives 24/3/49; fast gives 24/3/49; fast/stop/slow/fast/stop/fast/slow/fast gives 24/3/49.

Escape pauses (texts Paused, Resume, Title; clock stays 8). Enter on Resume continues from clock 8, and Title gives up with the ledger unchanged. But Escape in Paused never resumes: 400:escape, also with 'none' before and after, and 500/501/502:escape, left the screen paused up to tick 700.
After a finished night: ledger [{24,3,49,normal}] in state. A later run's Ledger screen showed 'Coins 40, served 5, lost 44, Normal' newest first. A fresh place's Ledger reads 'No nights yet'.
Four nights (normal, hard, easy, then a normal seed-3 night) left [40/5/44 normal, 64/8/45 easy, 8/1/51 hard]: the first was dropped. A given-up night and two replays added nothing.
After the night the title reads Layout, Replay, Ledger, Settings, Quit with replay_ready true, at once and in later runs on the same place.

Kept night (seed 1, normal, stove (0,0)/table (1,0), 24/3/49), replayed with seed 9, difficulty hard and a changed grid: night, replaying true, text 'Replay', arrivals the seed-1 list. The frame and the play use the kept grid (eating at 25). Summary: 'Replay over' 24/3/49. Ledger and Replay unchanged, and a second replay gave the same result.
After grid edits, save_slot/load_slot and switching to hard, Replay of the kept 40/5/44 night ended 'Replay over' 40/5/44. Grid change plus hard: 24/3/49 as the night had.
Two identical copies of one kept folder, seed 4, same script with --at: the outputs were byte-identical (cmp). Seeds 2 and 7 gave other arrivals.

Layout frame: 8x5 grid with a red stove at (0,0), a brown table at (2,0), a small yellow lamp at (2,1), and a white outline on the cursor cell (1,0); Piece, Slot and the stock texts shown. All match the state.

Night frame at minute 37: grid and pieces; customers eating (green) at (1,1), cooking (orange) at (1,3), seated (white) at (3,0); 2 queued blue squares at the left. Coins/Served/Lost/18:37/Speed: Slow shown. All match the state.

Frames of title (Replay marked), settings (Difficulty marked), ledger (3 lines, Back marked), paused (Resume marked) and summary (Night over, coins/served/lost, Enter: title marked) all show their texts.

README gives keys/how to play, says everything kept is in the --settings folder's settings.json, and its two commands (play and the --frame play) ran as written. It also admits the repeated-word limit.

defects: Headless input: a game word given again (at the next tick or later, with no different word between) acts only once. The brief says each word acts every time it is given; the README admits this.
Escape on the Paused screen does nothing (should resume).
During a replay the state's 'grid' key shows the current Layout grid, not the replayed night's grid. The frame and the play use the kept grid.
The night HUD panel shows a stray empty focused button below the speed line.
README notes that a word at the last tick (tick N with --ticks N) is refused, and that with --ticks 0 the kept things are not yet loaded.
On the summary, customers' 'wait' shows clock 360 minus arrival, a minute that was never played (cosmetic).

trace.how: context, new, read_again and how far the context grew are the run's own records. written_out a request is its growth less its answers (characters / 4), scaled to the run's exact total; of_which_unseen is that less the visible text (thinking). cost is what the request read and wrote, weighted; carried is what reading again what it added cost at every later request (start.carried: the same for what every request starts from). reading + writing is in_the_ledger
